blocks.content: The kind field declares exactly what type of object a manifest describes, this topic recaps every Kind covered throughout this entire course, in one place.
kind is the single field that tells Kubernetes, and anyone reading the manifest, exactly what kind of object this is, a Pod, a Deployment, a Service, and so on.

blocks.alt: One field, declaring exactly what the rest of the manifest actually describes

blocks.content: 2. Every Kind Covered in This Course
blocks.text: 2. Every Kind Covered in This Course

blocks.content: Across this entire course, you have encountered a genuinely wide range: Pod, Deployment, ReplicaSet, Service, Ingress, ConfigMap, Secret, PersistentVolume, PersistentVolumeClaim, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job, CronJob, Role, RoleBinding, and more, each with its own dedicated module.

blocks.alt: A genuinely wide range, each one covered in its own dedicated module throughout this course

blocks.content: Every kind value follows the exact same convention, PascalCase (Deployment, not deployment), and it is genuinely case-sensitive, getting the casing wrong will simply fail.

blocks.alt: A consistent, case-sensitive convention, worth getting exactly right

blocks.content: Neither field alone fully identifies a resource type, it is kind combined with apiVersion, covered in the previous topic, that together uniquely identify exactly which resource type a manifest describes.

blocks.alt: Two fields together, not either one alone, form the complete, unique identifier

blocks.content: kubectl api-resources lists every Kind actually available in your specific cluster, including any custom ones added by extensions, a direct, authoritative way to see the full picture rather than relying on memory alone.

blocks.alt: A direct, authoritative list from your own cluster, including anything added by extensions

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: kind declares the object type, following a consistent, case-sensitive PascalCase convention across every resource type covered throughout this course.
kind and apiVersion together, not either alone, uniquely identify a resource type, and kubectl api-resources shows every Kind actually available in your cluster.
